column2: Saul speaks to Jonathan and all servants about David's death, while Jonathan greatly favors David. The contrast is made audible by But without changing either actor.
Jonathan warns of Saul's seeking to kill and gives three protective instructions for tomorrow morning: guard yourself, hide and remain concealed.
Jonathan promises to stand beside his father in David's field, speak about David, observe and report; the repeated first-person commitments remain.
Jonathan's favorable report preserves the honorific shift from the king to your servant and direct you, followed by David's innocence and very good deeds.
column3: The unusual third-person royal title with second-person possession follows the Greek rather than being regularized into his servant.

column2: Soul in hand, striking the foreigner, the Lord's great deliverance and all Israel's seeing and joy precede the accusation of innocent blood and killing without cause.
Saul hears and swears a negative oath that David shall not die; the ei clause is read in its oath function, not as a positive prediction.
Jonathan reports all words and brings David back before Saul as formerly; the yesterday-and-third-day idiom is expressed as former days.
Renewed war is against Saul, David grows strong and deals a very great blow, and the foreigners flee. Again follows the repeated-event construction.
An evil spirit of God is upon sleeping Saul, with spear in hand while David plays with plural hands. Sleeping is retained rather than replaced by sitting.
column3: The physical setting and spirit attribution remain the narrator's wording, without an invented medical explanation.

column2: Saul seeks to strike with the spear, David moves away, the spear strikes the wall and David escapes. The inherited repeated names make the alternating subjects clear.
That night begins this unit's sending of watchers for a morning killing, followed by Michal's conditional warning to save one's own soul tonight. The chapter's time boundaries are retained.
Michal lowers David through the window; going away, fleeing and being saved remain three actions rather than a single summary escape.
Funerary images, bed, goats' liver at its head and covering with a garment remain in the selected sequence.
column3: Kenotaphia as funerary images and the singular head reference are provisional; liver is not changed to hair, and no physical mechanism for the deception is invented.

column2: Saul sends to take David, and an unnamed plural group says he is ill. The report is not reassigned directly to Michal where the selected verb is plural.
Saul sends for David with an instruction to bring him on the bed for execution; illness does not soften the stated purpose.
The messengers encounter the funerary images and goats' liver; there were carries the presentative force naturally. Both objects repeat the earlier setup.
Saul accuses Michal of deceiving him and releasing his enemy; she reports David threatening to kill her unless released. The threat is marked as her reported speech, not a narrator's confirmation.
David escapes to Samuel at Armathaim, reports all Saul's actions, and the pair stays at Nauath in Ramah. Both named travelers and the nested location remain.
The report to Saul explicitly presents David at Nauath in Ramah with Behold; the repeated location remains.
Messengers sent to seize David see the prophetic assembly under Samuel; God's Spirit comes on those messengers and they prophesy. Standing and appointed over them both remain.
Other messengers and then a third dispatch each also prophesy; the repeated outcome is retained without compressing the three missions.
Saul's intense anger, personal journey to Armathaim, well of the threshing floor at Sephi, inquiry and Behold reply all remain.
Saul goes toward Nauath in Ramah and prophesies under God's Spirit until arrival; the repeated start and end location and also upon him remain.
Saul removes his garments, prophesies before them and falls naked for the whole day and night; the ensuing proverb remains a question.
column3: Naked and the duration are retained without embellishment; the posture verb is not silently replaced with a diagnosis or different physical action.

column2: David's escape leads to three questions about deed, wrong and sin, followed by the father's seeking his soul. The increasing personal challenge remains.
Jonathan emphatically denies death, presents his father's practice of uncovering his ear about great or small matters, questions concealment and rejects the report. All negatives remain.
The father's sure knowledge of favor leads to a reported wish for Jonathan's ignorance, then the Lord's life and Jonathan's soul are invoked before the filled-space assertion.
column3: The space is supplied as an English subject for the impersonal filled construction; it is not replaced by a one-step-from-death idiom from another text. Lest he refuse interprets the negative willingness clause.

column2: Jonathan asks what David's soul desires and what he shall do; the two questions remain rather than an unconditional promise of anything whatever.
Behold introduces tomorrow's new moon, emphatic non-sitting with the king and the request to depart and hide until evening. No third-day ending is added to this unit.
The planned explanation cites David's earnest request to run to his city Bethlehem for the whole tribe's annual sacrifice.
column3: The father's inquiry also uses a cognate emphatic construction; inherited inquires expresses its action, while the rhetorical strength remains a possible refinement. No further sacrificial details are supplied.

column2: Good signifies peace for the servant, whereas a harsh reply indicates determined evil; both branches of the test and the father's agency remain.

Mercy is grounded in the Lord's covenant joining servant and Jonathan; conditional personal guilt leads to the demand that Jonathan himself kill David rather than bring him to his father. The repeated servant language remains.
Propose For before the explanatory conditional and know for certain for the emphatic knowing construction. The broken and if not, the danger from his father and reporting in your cities remain.
column3: The conditional sequence is syntactically incomplete; the dashes mark inherited uncertainty rather than reconstructing omitted words, and cities is not replaced with a different location.

column2: David asks who will report a harsh paternal answer; the question concerns communication, without supplying an unnamed messenger in advance.
Jonathan commands going and remaining in the field, and both go out there. The command is not silently replaced with a joint invitation absent from the selected wording.
Propose Behold at the introduction of the good report condition. The Lord's knowing, Jonathan's inquiry at a third time, good concerning David and sending to the field remain.
column3: The inherited shall I not send construes the negative as a rhetorical question; a conditional negative linked to the following self-curse is also possible. Source punctuation does not settle this, and the inherited interrogative remains explicitly provisional.

column2: The self-curse names Jonathan, then bringing evils upon David, uncovering his ear, sending away in peace and the Lord's presence as formerly with his father remain.
column3: Bringing the evils is an especially difficult selected expression; it is not silently changed to reporting evil or his father intending it. Its relation to the preceding oath needs specialist review.

column2: Mercy while Jonathan lives is followed by a possible emphatic dying, with the condition continuing into verse 15; no unattested question is inserted.
Never removing mercy from Jonathan's house precedes the Lord's removal of each enemy and the oath-like continuation into verse 16.
column3: May it not be interprets ei me with the following infinitive as a negative wish/oath construction; the clause linkage remains provisional.

column2: The desired preservation of Jonathan's name in David's house is followed by the Lord's seeking David's enemies. No covenant-making verb is inserted in place of the selected removal language.
Jonathan swears again because he loved the soul of the one loving him; the reciprocal relation is retained instead of recasting it as David swearing or Jonathan loving him as his own soul.
Tomorrow's new moon leads to being sought because the seat will be inspected; the repeated inspection vocabulary remains rather than all occurrences becoming empty.
Doing a third time, looking about, returning to the working-day hiding place and sitting by the ergab remain.
column3: The first two verbs and ergab are opaque; the text is not silently reconstructed into wait three days and go quickly to a named stone.

column2: Jonathan will act three times with shafts, hurling toward the amattari; the opaque target term remains without a new identification.
Propose Behold instead of Then to retain the explicit presentative before sending the boy. The singular shaft, nearer-side signal, instruction to take it, David's coming and sworn peace remain.
column3: No danger interprets no word/matter in the signal context; it is not a separate Greek noun for danger.

column2: The farther-side signal means departure because the Lord has sent David away; the divine sending and contrast with the nearer signal remain.
The spoken word between the two is placed under the Lord as witness for ever, with Behold and both persons explicit.
David hides, the month arrives and the king approaches the table to eat; the selected month expression is retained without a reconstructed festival ritual.
The king's usual wall seat, preceding Jonathan, Abner beside Saul and inspection of David's place remain.
column3: Preceded follows proephthasen; the relationship of arrival, seating and precedence is not fully resolved by the running text alone.

column2: Saul's silence is explained by his supposition of an occurrence and lack of purification. The repeated uncleanness/purification language remains.
column3: Occurrence for symptoma leaves the unspecified cause open rather than inventing an accidental bodily event.

column2: On the month's second day the seat is again inspected, and Saul asks Jonathan why Jesse's son has missed both yesterday and today. Both days remain.
Jonathan reports David's request to go to Bethlehem, his city, introducing the fuller explanation in the next unit.
The reported request cites tribal sacrifice, plural brothers' command, favor in Jonathan's eyes and seeing the brothers; the explanatory return to the king's table closes the report.
Saul's intense anger produces the selected plural insult son of deserting girls and an accusation of companionship bringing shame and maternal exposure.
column3: The insult's force and irregular grammar remain open; it is not replaced by a familiar singular insult or modern slur.

column2: Propose For at the explanation of threatened kingship and So now for the inferential command. Jesse's son's lifetime, fetching the young man and son of death remain.
Jonathan asks why David should die and what he has done; the two questions challenge sentence and grounds separately.
Saul raises the spear to kill Jonathan, who recognizes the determination to kill David. The two intended victims and recognition's object remain clear.
Jonathan leaps from the table in fierce anger and refuses bread on the second day, crushed over David because his father had determined against him.
column3: The final pronoun is not explicitly renamed; David is contextually likely, but the grammatical compression and unstated object of determined remain open.

column2: Morning travel to the field follows the arrangement for David's testimony, with a little boy accompanying Jonathan.
column3: Testimony for martyrion remains provisional; it is not silently converted into an agreed appointment without noting the selected noun.

column2: Propose naming Jonathan as the inferred shaft-throwing subject after the boy runs, making the actor switch audible. Plural requested shafts and the singular shaft sent past remain.
The boy reaches the shaft's place and Jonathan calls the farther-side signal after him; the signal reproduces the planned direction.
Quickly, hurry and do not stand still retain the urgent clustered commands; the boy gathers plural shafts for his master.
The boy's complete ignorance contrasts with only Jonathan and David knowing; only is supported by the explicit exception parex.
Jonathan gives his equipment to his boy and sends him into the city; the repeated boy references preserve the controlled separation before David appears.
After the boy enters, David rises from the ergab, falls on his face and bows three times; mutual kissing and weeping continue until a great completion.
column3: Completion remains an unresolved abstract endpoint, not silently changed to David weeping more; ergab retains its earlier opaque form.

column2: The peaceful departure invokes both men's oath, the Lord as witness between the men and between their seed for ever. Departure actions assigned to 21:1 are not moved into this unit.
